critical_evidence.evidence: No borescope or rebuild invoice. Seller's mechanic 'did not recommend the quite invasive pan removal method borescope' and cited only symptom absence (no tick, no oil use, no soot). A standard borescope goes through the spark-plug holes and is not invasive, so the stated reason does not hold up. Symptom reports are not evidence of clean cylinder walls.

A DME report is in the gallery (not examined here); the seller calls it 'good looking'. The same dealer's September 2026 BaT listing for this VIN disclosed one Range 5 over-rev that the seller could not explain. This needs specialist interpretation, including whether the event was ignition-only and at what engine hours.

Listing summarises a gallery invoice: water pump, thermostat and serpentine belt in Apr 2023 at 47,159 mi, after a reported pulley failure. Transmission fluid Mar 2022; regular oil changes. No AOS, coolant-pipe, coolant-flush, spark-plug or clutch records are cited. Invoices not examined here.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are present: VIN, clean CA title claim, Carfax, build sheet, and a reserve auction with a stated close. Maintenance invoices cover 2022-2026 including the water pump, plus a DME report. Missing: records for the first ~40k miles and 14 years, AOS and coolant-pipe history, and any borescope. The DME report carries a previously disclosed Range 5 event.

condition.rationale: Photos show a tidy exterior and well-kept leather. The listing discloses chips, scratches and interior touch-point wear. Two new tires and 2024 brakes are documented by summary. Engine condition, the most important item on an M97, is unproven: no borescope, an unexplained Range 5 over-rev, and a 2023 pulley failure with unknown overheating.

price_value.rationale: The $30,000 bid sits at the fair-value mid of $29,934 (range $26,691-$32,896). The prior reserve-not-met at $32,500 implies the reserve sits at or above the top of that range. The S premium is not supported by engine due diligence, and the open over-rev question pulls value down.

mission_fit.rationale: Keeper-category car with the right transmission. The profile allows a 3.4 S only with unusually strong engine due diligence, which this listing lacks. The likely hammer price is well above the ideal $10k-$19k band and works against cash preservation.

logistics.rationale: Hawthorne is roughly a day's drive from Carmel. It is a CA-registered stock car and the dealer offers to coordinate a PPI. With about one day before close, a specialist PPI plus borescope before bidding is tight. Sales tax applies on in-state delivery as a cost item.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Six-speed manual Cayman S in Midnight Blue over extended Natural Brown leather is a genuinely desirable combination. Aftermarket crest badges on the console and glove box detract slightly.

evidence.mission_note: As a future keeper it has the right spec and colour combination, but the profile requires unusually strong engine due diligence on a 3.4 S, and that is absent here. The likely price sits far above the ideal band and works against cash preservation.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a VIN-confirmed 2008 Cayman S six-speed with a clean CA title claim, a Carfax, a build sheet, and gallery invoices from 2022-2026, including a 2023 water pump/thermostat/belt job and regular oil services. Observed issues are disclosed chips, scratches and interior wear, plus aftermarket crest badges noted in the comments. The decisive open item is engine health. The same dealer's prior BaT listing disclosed an unexplained Range 5 over-rev, which this listing omits. The seller declined a borescope on an inaccurate premise. The 2023 pulley failure may have involved overheating the seller cannot rule out. AOS, coolant pipes, plugs, clutch and the first ~40k miles of history are undocumented. The current $30,000 bid matches the fair-value mid, and the prior $32,500 reserve-not-met suggests the hammer will land near or above the top of the fair range.
